question: Why did the dotted H19-5 d=2.8 raster (mirrored at GEMSDOE25 docs/downloads, owner-reported 0.2600; public leaderboard row wbg1 #15 = 0.2600 observed 2026-10-03) score highest of the local family, and can a higher score be designed?
claim_hygiene: 0.2600 is an owner-reported / public-leaderboard-row figure and is not an organizer receipt for these bytes. Links between the local file, the owner and the leaderboard row are unproven.

relations.reading: all three rasters are the same detector emission (H19-5) at different packing distances; the d=2.8-class file is a deterministic thinning of the same bytes.

metric_algebra.official_definition: DTI = TPw/(TPw + 0.2 FPw + 0.8 FNw); k(d)=max(1-d/300m,0); alpha=0.2, beta=0.8 (DrivenData #306 problem page)
metric_algebra.exact_rearrangement: with A = TPw (sum over truth of the best nearby prediction), B = sum over predictions of the best nearby truth, T = truth count and N = emitted count: DTI = A/(0.8T + 0.2N + 0.2(A-B)). When A and B are equal (a one-to-one matching) this is DTI = A/(0.8T + 0.2N)
metric_algebra.marignal_rule: dropping one emitted pixel whose own kernel credit is a raises DTI iff a < 0.2*DTI; adding one raises DTI iff its expected kernel mass exceeds 0.2*DTI. At DTI 0.2477 the break-even is 0.0495, at 0.26 it is 0.052, at 0.3195 it is 0.064
metric_algebra.binary_optimality: for a fixed support, DTI is monotone non-decreasing in each p(x) whenever that pixel's expected credit exceeds the break-even, and the ratio is linear in each p, so the optimum is attained at the corners p in {0,1}: soft probability fields cannot beat the best binary set under the initial-round metric
metric_algebra.used_by_submission: the shipped artifacts are binary {0,1} rasters, consistent with this

calibration.method: closed-form solve of the two-parameter emission model on the two reported anchors (solid 0.1922, dotted d=1.5 0.2477) using measured dot counts and the sibling's geometric retention curve; the d=2.8-class file is then predicted out of sample
calibration.verdict: the model calibrated on two anchors predicts 0.4064 for the third file; the reported value 0.2600 lies inside the sibling's published interval [0.2500, 0.2613], i.e. the emission-geometry model transfers out of sample

targets.truth_size_note: |G| is not observable from here. 12,630 px is the sibling's lattice calibration (unconfirmed); 20,000 px is shown as a sensitivity.
targets.reading: with the current credit fraction held fixed, 0.3195 requires ~20919 emitted pixels instead of 44090 - i.e. the same fault mass concentrated in ~half the dots - or, at the current dot count, credit must rise from 0.386 to 0.511 of the hidden truth (-+32%). Both routes are ranking problems, not geometry problems.

catalogue_stand_in.note: the published catalogue is the only local truth-like mask; it is NOT the hidden test set, and these rows are descriptive only
